title: FairShare admission controller for tiered routing with quota-aware prioritization and model-variant fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a FairShare Admission Controller that enforces tier-based routing policies across free, paid, and enterprise tiers while being quota-aware and supporting fallback to cheaper model variants. The controller must: 1) allocate admission capacity based on configurable tier weights and per-tenant budgets, 2) smooth bursts to meet latency SLOs using a leaky-bucket-style admission window per tier, 3) allow graceful demotion to cheaper model variants when a request would be throttled, and 4) respect regional affinity and data-residency constraints when selecting fallbacks. Goal: reduce user-visible 429s for paid and enterprise customers while keeping acceptable latency and minimizing extra cost on host capacity.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller enforces per-tier fair-share weights and prevents starvation of paid/enterprise tiers under bursty free-tier load
Fallbacks to cheaper model variants are executed with configurable hysteresis and do not exceed quality-regression threshold defined in model-evals
End-to-end 95th percentile latency for routed requests stays within current SLO (+10% tolerance) during 2x traffic bursts in staging
Observed 429 rate for paid tier <= 0.1% under simulated mixed traffic at 120% baseline load
rollout_plan: Deploy to canary cluster handling 1% of traffic, run synthetic mixed-tier load for 48h
Progressively increase to 10% then 50% with automated rollback on SLO breaches
Monitor fallback rates, latency, and token-costs for first 7 days before full rollout
implementation_notes: Admission uses a weighted token budget where each tier receives weight*global_budget tokens per epoch; tokens are consumed proportional to cost_estimate(token_count, model_variant)
Maintain per-tenant sliding-window utilisation to avoid letting a single tenant exhaust tier allocation; implement soft caps with backoff before hard deny
Fallback decisions use a ranked model-variant list with quality deltas; only demote if fallback quality delta < configured threshold and token savings > threshold
Regional preference: prefer fallbacks in same region; if unavailable, use cross-region fallback only for non-data-resident requests or with customer opt-in
testing_notes: Create mixed-tier synthetic workload generator (free:60%, paid:30%, enterprise:10%) with varied prompt sizes to validate smoothing and admission fairness
Run chaos test where multiple free-tier tenants burst simultaneously to ensure paid/enterprise priority preserved
Add unit tests for budget arithmetic and hysteresis timers; e2e integration test against local runtime and k8s autoscaler
engineering_updates: 2026-03-02 - Initial design doc posted to Confluence (link above). Waiting on product trade-off for allowable fallback quality delta.
2026-03-05 - Prototype admission window implemented; local sims show ~40% reduction in paid-tier 429s in synthetic tests.
2026-03-08 - Review feedback from PM: add explicit per-tenant soft-eviction policy and observable counters for tenant-level fairness. Assigned to Marco for follow-up.

2026-03-11 - Hooked up preliminary fallback ranking with model-evals scores; observed some corner cases where demotions increase latency due to model size differences. Investigating prefetching smaller models' KV caches as mitigation.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Aggressive demotion causes unacceptable quality regressions for enterprise customers. Mitigation: require per-customer opt-in and per-customer quality budget; default enterprise demotion disabled.

Risk: Regional fallback increases egress and adds compliance exposure. Mitigation: block cross-region fallbacks for customers with data residency requirements and add explicit audit logs for any cross-region decision.
Risk: Admission algorithm misconfig leads to paid-tier starvation. Mitigation: add automated alerts on paid-tier throttled rate and enforce minimal guaranteed token-share for paid/enterprise tiers.

Implement per-tenant soft-eviction logic and expose config via console for trials
